title: Pneumococcal vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that protects against pneumococcus, a common cause of severe pneumonia, ear infections, and meningitis.
why: For children on the schedule from the first months of life. For adults, usually after 65, and with heart or lung disease or diabetes.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If you are ill now or have a fever
Which pneumococcal vaccines you have already had

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are well.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: There are different vaccines, and the schedule depends on age. Your doctor will choose.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that makes it easy to uncover your upper arm.

steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in your documents
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes soreness or redness at the spot for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes tiredness or a mild fever
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
You can go back to normal activities
Your doctor will say if another dose is needed
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services

faq.q: Does it protect against all pneumonia?
faq.a: No, only pneumococcal pneumonia. But it is one of the most common and dangerous causes.

faq.q: Can I get it with my flu shot?
faq.a: Usually yes, on the same day. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Pneumococcal vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
